reason: The text contains several named characters who function as regular people. Most notably, Rebekah (רִבְקָה) is introduced as an ordinary young woman from a family—she draws water, comes from a household, and is described in mundane, relatable terms before her elevation through marriage. Similarly, Laban (לָבָן), her brother, is presented as a regular family member managing household affairs. Even Abraham's servant (עֶבֶד), while holding authority over the household, is depicted as performing ordinary tasks and responding to daily circumstances, functioning as a regular person despite his elevated position within the household.
